newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower on exports, commercial sales.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower on exports, commercial sales.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on bearish input from the export sector plus aggressive commercial selling, traders said.
But trading was quiet and volume was thin with the market awaiting the USDA final 1996 U.S. crop production report slated for release Friday at 0730 CST, traders said.
"There's not a lot happening, just waiting for the report," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
An average of analysts' estimates pegged the 1996 U.S. corn production tally to be 9.317 billion bushels, up from the government's previous forecast for 9.265 billion bushels.

The corn market was caught between a bearish export report and a bullish farmer selling scenario. "Farmers want three dollar (per bushel) corn and are holding out for that but I don't think they're going to get it," a trader said.
USDA early Thursday said U.S. net export sales of corn for the week ended January 2 totaled 236,800 tonnes, below trade expectations for 400,000 to 600,000 tonnes.
"It was a holiday week but that's even low for a holiday week," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co of that week's sales.
Corn closed unchanged to 1-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with March down one at $2.58-1/4.
Contract lows were set with the new low for May at $2.58 per bushel, down from the previous low of $2.58-1/2 set Wednesday.
The commercial selling centered on Cargill Inc's sale of at least ten million bushels, 3.5 million in the March and 6.5 million in the July contract, traders said.
FIMAT Futures bought two million March, Griffin Trading bought three million bushels of March and Tenco Inc sold 3.5 million bushels of March, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 51,000 contracts, below the 56,306 traded Wednesday, according to the CBOT.

In corn options, Farmers Commodities Corp bought 300 March $2.90 calls at 1/2 cent, FIMAT Futures sold 200 March $2.60 calls at five cents and USA Trading sold 200 May $3.00 calls at 1-1/4 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 11,000 contracts, below the 15,373 traded Wednesday.
In spread trading, Cargill Inc did two million bushels of May/March at even money and Cargill Investor Services along with Refco Inc did one million March/May at even money, traders said.
